issue.title: UnsupportedOperationException: View 'unix' not available

repository.name: testcontainers-java
repository.description: Testcontainers is a Java library that supports JUnit tests, providing lightweight, throwaway instances of common databases, Selenium web browsers, or anything else that can run in a Docker container.

body:
I've managed to track this down to what looks like a race condition, introduced when we changed the selenium container wait strategy to be based on log output. It occurs at this line in `containerIsStarted`:
```
        this.driver = new RemoteWebDriver(getSeleniumAddress(), desiredCapabilities);
```
I see a thread blocked reading a socket inside of selenium's RemoteWebDriver. I imagine we're trying to initialise the driver too quickly now, and we're hitting this intermittently.

I'll try to resolve by wrapping the affected line inside of a timeout-and-retry construct.
@rnorth 👍 if it fixes this annoying freezing, that would be awesome!

issue.title: BrowserWebDriverContainer: Timeout in containerIsStarted

repository.name: testcontainers-java
repository.description: Testcontainers is a Java library that supports JUnit tests, providing lightweight, throwaway instances of common databases, Selenium web browsers, or anything else that can run in a Docker container.

issue.body: We get a timeout in BrowserWebDriverContainer#containerIsStarted. It seems the fix for #373 is broken. The inner getWithTimout contains a double nested lambda so the timeout is only applied to the outer lambda which returns immediatly. So when "new RemoteWebDriver" gets stuck in the race condition mentioned in #373, retryUntilSuccess throws when it reaches its own timeout in the first try.
